summary:
The Furniture Industry Sustainability Programme (FISP) marked its 20th anniversary on 7 October with an event at Furniture Makers' Hall in London, gathering scheme members, industry representatives and stakeholders to mark two decades of work promoting responsible business practice in the furniture sector. Guests were welcomed by Joanna Knight, Chair of the FISP Steering Committee and editor of Sustainability Works, who reviewed the scheme's achievements and thanked members for their continued support.

A panel of long-standing members reflected on the value of membership. Participants were Fiona Edwards (JPA Workspaces), Lauren Thompson (Orangebox), Ursula Bytnar (Task Systems), Natalie Goodwin (Sealy) and Andy Barham (Premiere Kitchens). They discussed how sustainability expectations have shifted over time and how FISP supported their businesses in responding to changing customer, market and regulatory demands, and argued the scheme remains relevant for demonstrating responsible business credentials.

John Hubbard, FISP Technical Lead and Sustainability Expert at Fira-International, set out the scheme's next chapter, covering the changing legislative landscape, plans to introduce an associate membership category, and opportunities to widen participation in the domestic furniture sector.

Knight said celebrating 20 years was a proud milestone and credited members and supporters, adding that FISP remains focused on helping businesses navigate change, share best practice and demonstrate commitment to responsible business. The evening closed with networking, drinks and canapes. As it enters its third decade, FISP says it will continue to provide a practical framework for continuous improvement and industry collaboration as new sustainability challenges emerge. The article is a trade association milestone piece rather than analysis, with no data on membership numbers or environmental outcomes. Image credit: Orangebox.
